data.title: Evaluation of resveratrol, green tea extract, curcumin, oxaloacetic acid, and medium-chain triglyceride oil on life span of genetically heterogeneous mice
data.authors: Strong R; Miller RA; Harrison DE et al.
data.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: None of five popular longevity compounds had a statistically significant effect on lifespan. The paper explicitly states the ITP's mission is to publish all results, positive or negative - the exact registry model this Atlas should emulate.
data.abstract_excerpt: The National Institute on Aging Interventions Testing Program (ITP) was established to evaluate agents that are hypothesized to increase life span and/or health span in genetically heterogeneous mice. Each compound is tested in parallel at three test sites. It is the goal of the ITP to publish all results, negative or positive.

extracted_findings.intervention: Resveratrol, green tea extract, curcumin, oxaloacetic acid, MCT oil (dietary)
extracted_findings.effect: Lifespan test: these compounds did not robustly extend lifespan (largely negative ITP result)
